White Win Probability by Rating Differential

Rating gap is decisive: When white holds a 300+ point rating advantage, white wins at an extremely high rate. Conversely, when black has a 300+ point advantage, white's win probability drops sharply below 50%. The crossover point is near 0 differential, where white still maintains a slight edge from the first-move advantage.

Time control and game length: Classical games run substantially longer than blitz or bullet games. Rapid and classical formats also show higher checkmate rates — players are less likely to resign when they have time to find defensive resources.
Section 06

Key Findings & Strategic Takeaways

Tight synthesis of the six most actionable insights from this dataset.

52.3%

First-Move Advantage is Real

White wins 52.3% of decisive games across this entire dataset. The 4.7pp gap over black holds across every rating bracket and time control tested, confirming structural first-move advantage.

55.6%

Resignations Dominate

55.6% of games end in resignation, compared to 31.5% checkmates and 8.4% timeouts. At all rating levels players prefer to resign over fighting to mate.

85%

Rating Differential is the Best Predictor

White with a 300+ rating advantage wins over 85% of decisive games. Conversely, when black has a 300+ point edge, white win rate falls below 17%.

227

Opening Diversity is High

227 distinct opening families appear in the dataset. The top 15 openings account for the plurality of games, with win rates varying by several percentage points — meaningful for preparation.

4

Openings Can Flip the Advantage

Among the top 15 openings, 4 show black outperforming white on win rate. Opening choice is therefore one of black's primary tools for neutralizing white's structural edge.

65 vs 54

Game Length Reveals Quality

Checkmate games average 65.4 turns while resignations average 53.9 turns. Classical time controls produce the longest games; bullet produces the shortest. Higher-rated games also tend to run longer.

Analyst Summary

This dataset of 20,058 Lichess games confirms that the first-move advantage — white winning 52.3% of decisive games — is the single most consistent structural signal. Rating differential amplifies or overwhelms this advantage: a 300+ point rating gap is the decisive factor in the outcome roughly 85% of the time when white holds it. Blitz is the dominant time control (9.6% of games), and resignation is the dominant termination type (55.6%), reflecting pragmatic play at all levels. For players looking to improve their results with black, opening selection is actionable — several top-15 openings tilt win rates in black's favor.
